Subject: Renewal proposal: BrightRoute reserved pool + HW class update

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the renewal conversation last week. Per our call, I’m putting a short written proposal together so your procurement and infra teams have something to review. High-level ask from BrightRoute: renew Dedicated Reserved capacity for Q4 2026 with an increase of +16 GPUs and move to a mixed hardware pool (A100 -> H100 for burst/critical latency, L40S for steady-state throughput where it’s more cost-efficient).

Proposal summary (attached: BrightRoute_NewQuote_9-14.pdf; benchmark CSV attached):
- Term: 12 months (start 2026-11-01) with option to extend at 6/12 month renewals.
- Capacity: +16 GPUs (we recommend 8x H100 + 8x L40S reserved pool).
- Throughput guarantee: minimum sustained throughput target of 9k tokens/sec aggregate (route-level SLOs included).
- Pricing: blended reserved rate; see attached quote for line items and commitment tiers.
- Support: 24x7 incident escalation + 30-day throughput regression monitoring during first month.

Next steps I propose:
1) Can your procurement review the attached quote and return any required PO template or redlines?
2) If infra wants more depth on perf-per-dollar, I’ll loop in Marcus (cc’d) to share the raw benchmarking and short perf runbook.
3) Book a 30-min call this week to lock terms and timeline.

I’ve attached a CSV with our benchmark runs comparing A100 vs H100 vs L40S on a representative BrightRoute workload (with your sample prompt mix). Marcus will annotate the numbers.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Hi Samir — quick answers and I’ve looped in Marcus from Applied ML for the perf details (see his note later in thread):
- Cost delta: the attached quote includes a blended per-GPU reserved price and an example $/1k token illustration. Ballpark: the blended H100+L40S pool is ~12–18% lower $/token vs A100-only for BrightRoute’s workload mix (sustained throughput scenarios) because L40S offers better FP16 inference throughput per dollar at higher batch sizes.
- Routing/failover: Redwood supports policy-based routing. You can pin latency-sensitive routes to H100 instances. If H100 capacity is saturated, the system can automatically fall back to compatible H100-quantized variants or route to L40S with a configurable degradation policy (priority: H100 pool -> H100-quantized -> L40S). We’ll include a fallback playbook in the SOW.
- PO/SOW: attached SOW-dedicated-pool-v2.docx is a PO-ready draft. If procurement needs specific contract language, we can accept a redline.

Can we schedule a 30-min call Thursday morning PT for Marcus to walk through the CSV numbers live? Lauren — could you please share available slots?

Subject: Fwd: Renewal proposal — technical notes and perf-per-dollar justification

Hi Samir — Marcus from Applied ML here. I ran the benchmark matrix referenced in the CSV against BrightRoute’s sample prompt mix (70% generation, 30% rerank/embeddings) with realistic sequence lengths. Quick summary of measured medians (see attached CSV for full runs):

- Latency (median per-token latency on generation tasks): A100 (p4) = 0.78 ms/token; H100 = 0.42 ms/token; L40S = 0.55 ms/token.
- Throughput (tokens/sec, single GPU, mixed batch sizes): A100 = 7.1k; H100 = 11.9k; L40S = 10.2k.
- Cost per effective token (normalized to A100 baseline): A100 = 1.0; H100 = 0.95; L40S = 0.74.

Interpretation and recommendation:
- H100 gives the best latency and highest peak throughput per card, but has a higher reserved unit cost. L40S offers the best cost-per-token for sustained, batched workloads. For BrightRoute’s mix, a hybrid 8x H100 + 8x L40S pool reduces blended $/token by ~15% vs an A100-only renewal while improving tail latencies for critical routes.
- Routing model: pin critical routes to an H100 subset. Non-critical batch workloads route to the L40S nodes via the routing policy. During spikes, if H100 is saturated, automatic fallback rules can (a) shift low-priority traffic to L40S, and (b) pop additional H100 burst capacity if enabled in the contract. We can set a soft SLO for warm KV-cache hit rates and ensure prefix caching for recurring prompts which further reduces effective cost.

Operational ask if you proceed:
1) Confirm desired split (we recommend 8H100 / 8L40S).
2) Confirm throughput SLO target (we used 9k tokens/sec aggregate for pricing).
3) Fill in procurement PO template and target start date so we can schedule a drain/migration window.

I’ve attached the CSV and included a short appendix in the SOW draft with rollback/fallback configs. Happy to walk through the numbers on the call.

—Marcus Lin
Applied ML — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
